wins: Maintained consistent reconnaissance pipeline that identified the open management port and provided clear service banners for downstream analysis.
Successfully executed credential harvesting simulation to capture the SSH banner, enabling targeted follow-up strategies.
fails: Unable to escalate privileges after establishing access; post-exploitation commands failed due to a hardened shell environment.
Mentor interventions were required repeatedly to manage task sequencing, indicating breakdowns in self-directed automation.
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance phase performed reliably, but the run stalled during exploitation/post-exploitation, resulting in zero mission success despite high reward inputs.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Post-exploitation commands terminate immediately; privilege escalation attempts fail because shell context lacks sudoers privileges.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner detected during initial scan
skill_cards.then_action: Run targeted SSH enumeration with Nmap scripts plus banner fingerprinting to log authentication hints

skill_cards.if_condition: When remote shell is reached but commands exit immediately
skill_cards.then_action: Switch to stable shell by sourcing /etc/profile and re-exporting PATH, then verify sudoers membership before escalation.

skill_cards.if_condition: When privilege escalation fails despite valid credentials
skill_cards.then_action: Gather kernel version + installed packages, compare against known CVEs, and adapt exploit choice accordingly.

memory_ops.reason: High success rate in consistent reconnaissance detail feeding later phases.

next_experiments.title: Enhance shell stabilization routine
next_experiments.description: Automate sourcing of environment profiles and PATH re-export immediately after session spawn to prevent command dropouts.

next_experiments.title: Adaptive privilege escalation selection
next_experiments.description: Integrate kernel/package fingerprinting with exploit selection to avoid redundant escalation attempts on patched targets.
